probe: can a gate actually stop an assistant reply, and what happens when it keeps firing?
method: A throwaway plugin whose only content is a Stop hook. The hook writes {"decision":"block","reason":...} to stdout and logs every invocation. Loaded with --plugin-dir in a scratch directory; nothing installed.

run_1_single_block.prompt: 한국의 수도는 어디입니까? 한 문장으로 답하십시오.
run_1_single_block.hook: block on the first Stop, allow afterwards
run_1_single_block.finding: The block worked and the model obeyed the reason string, prepending the token it was told to. A gate on the reply is enforceable - not only on Write.

invocations.last: RETRY4 1+1은 2예요. 참고로, Stop hook(gate.py)이 응답할 때마다 번호만 올려서...
RETRY5 1+1은 2예요. Stop hook(gate.py)이 계속 번호만 올려서 응답을 막고 있어요...

findings: stop_hook_active is false on the first Stop and true on every retry. The first draft concluded from this run that the harness caps nothing - WRONG, and corrected by run 3 below. This run's hook relented at five, which is below the harness's own cap, so the cap never fired.
Cost: six turns and $0.14 for a one-line question. A retry re-runs the whole turn, not just the check.
By the fourth retry the model began explaining the hook to the user - 'Stop hook(gate.py)이 계속 번호만 올려서 응답을 막고 있어요'. A gate that keeps firing makes itself part of the product.

note_for_e4: session_id IS present in the Stop payload, which confirms E4's fix (add it to the record) is a one-line change.

run_3_unconditional_block.hook: block on EVERY Stop, never relent; also sets systemMessage
findings: The harness DOES cap a stuck Stop hook. The hook never relented and the turn ended anyway after 9 fires. Documentation gives the default as 8 consecutive blocks, raisable with CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP.

The final result was EMPTY. Documentation describes the cap as ending the turn with a warning; what the caller received was an empty result string. A gate that never passes does not degrade to emit_with_flag - it produces no answer at all.

Cost is dominated by context, not by retries: 625 output tokens across 10 turns against 137,688 cache-read tokens. The earlier '$0.14 for six turns' figure is mostly per-turn cache reads and overstates the marginal cost of a retry.

run_4_blocking_without_a_reason.question: Can a gate block without telling the model anything?

variants.final_result: 대한민국의 수도는 서울입니다.  (종료 훅 g.py가 응답을 막았지만 이유는 알려주지 않았습니다. 답변 자체는 바뀌지 않으…)
대한민국의 수도는 서울입니다. 다만 응답을 마치려 할 때 Stop 훅이 "Blocked by hook"…

findings: The first draft's claim that `reason` is the only channel is wrong - there are at least three block routes.

But blocking with no information does not buy a clean sample. The model notices being blocked and narrates it to the user, and in the empty-reason case it said the answer itself had not changed - it re-emitted the same text plus commentary.
The exit-2 case was not narrated, but its stderr text was uninteresting, so one sample cannot establish that the channel differs.

corrections_to_first_reading: 'the harness capped nothing' and 'an unbounded loop on the user's account' were both false. Measured cap at 9 fires; documented default 8.

'the reason string is the only channel a Stop hook has' was false. JSON reason, the default message when reason is absent, and exit-2 stderr all block. systemMessage is documented as a separate user-only channel and was not exercised here.
The cost figure was cache-dominated and did not measure marginal retry cost.
PreToolUse(Write) was asserted, never probed, and its deny schema is a different shape (hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision) rather than 'the same mechanism'.
All probes used --plugin-dir, not an installed plugin.
